summary.headline: Siyaram Q4 FY26 total income rose 16.1% YoY to INR 871 crores, PAT up 30.6% to INR 95 crores; FY27 revenue growth guided at about 12%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone total income was INR 871 crores (up 16.1% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 152 crores (17.4% margin, up 21%) and PAT of INR 95 crores (up 30.6%). Full-year FY26 total income reached INR 2,653 crores (up 15.5%), EBITDA INR 413 crores (15.6% margin) and PAT INR 228 crores (up 14.8%). Management said demand improved gradually in Q4 on wedding and festive season, while input-cost volatility and geopolitics remain a concern. The company announced a special interim dividend of INR 4 and final dividend of INR 5 per share (INR 16 total for FY26), plus a small residential project at Dombivali. Store count reached 44 (27 ZECODE, 17 DEVO), with a target of about 70 by FY27 end.

financial_highlights.value: INR 16 per share (special interim INR 4 + final INR 5 plus other components per management)

segments.name: Fabric
segments.commentary: About 80% of FY26 revenue. Volume grew about 10% and value about 11%, with management attributing growth mainly to market share gains and a favourable wedding season.

segments.name: Garments (ex-retail)
segments.commentary: About 15% of FY26 revenue. Volume grew about 9% and value about 8%, excluding the new retail business.

segments.name: Retail (ZECODE and DEVO)
segments.commentary: Company-owned stores, 44 at quarter end (27 ZECODE, 17 DEVO). FY26 retail revenue about INR 80 crores, with EBITDA drag within the guided 150 bps. Target of about 70 stores by FY27 end.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 10% of revenue in FY26, stable at 9-10% over recent years. Management did not give a share target.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 12%.
EBITDA margin guided at about 14%, with about 150 bps drag from retail; management cautioned this is subject to volatile input prices.
Store count to reach about 70 (ZECODE and DEVO) by end of FY27, implying about 26 additions, of which about 8 DEVO and the rest ZECODE; all company-owned (COCO), no franchising this year.
FY27 capex about INR 100 crores: INR 50-60 crores maintenance plus about INR 40 crores for new stores.
Ad spend guided at 4-5% of revenue.

Residential project at Dombivali (about 77,000 sq ft) to start June 2026, about 24 months; total outlay about INR 45-60 crores (incl. land per one reply), revenue about INR 80 crores; about INR 25 crores spend in FY27.

Preferential issue of RPS: NCLT final hearing done 16 April; order expected first week of June 2026, with about 3-4 months more to issue RPS. Management said RPS issue will not affect cash flows this year.
New ZECODE geographies planned in FY27: Bangalore radius, Chennai/Tamil Nadu, Hyderabad, south Maharashtra.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex about INR 100 crores: INR 50-60 crores regular maintenance plus about INR 40 crores for about 26 new stores.
Inventory per new company-owned store about INR 60-70 lakh.
Inventory days about 135-138 at March, similar to last year per management.
Dombivali residential project about 77,000 sq ft built-up, construction from June 2026, 24-month timeline; not treated as capex but as cash outflow.
Store sizes shifting to 6,000-10,000 sq ft (average about 7,000-8,000 sq ft) from earlier 4,000-5,000 sq ft.
demand_pricing: Management said consumer demand improved gradually in Q4, helped by income tax relief, wedding and festive season.
Raw material prices volatile; pass-through to consumers is gradual to protect volumes and market share.
Management expects branded players to gain share as input prices rise and the branded-unbranded gap narrows; said this is a longer-term play.
Legacy fabric business expected to grow high single digit to low double digit in FY27.
Q1 flagged as seasonally weakest quarter; management also cited geopolitics, raw material issues and heat wave.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 capex and store guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 100 crores capex: INR 50-60 crores maintenance plus about INR 40 crores for stores, taking the count to about 70 by year end.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin guidance be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: No change; management retained about 14% EBITDA margin guidance with 150 bps retail drag, subject to input price volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Retail FY26 revenue and margin drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail revenue about INR 80 crores versus INR 70-80 crores estimate; EBITDA drag was within the 150 bps budget. FY27 drag again guided at about 1.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why were FY26 store openings short of guidance (35 planned)?
qa_highlights.answer: Lean start-up team focused on operations; some sites were under-construction properties, delaying openings. FY27 target set more conservatively at about 70 total stores.

qa_highlights.question: Growth split between market share and channel inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was largely market share gain, with favourable wedding season; fabric market grows only a small percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory and debtors rise about 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly new stores (inventory held on books), partly build-up ahead of a strong Q4; inventory days stable at about 135-138. Operating cash flow about INR 150 crores, with large part absorbed by inventory and debtors.

qa_highlights.question: Other income composition for FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest about INR 27 crores, profit on sale of assets about INR 21 crores, MTM gain about INR 12.73 crores, capital subsidy INR 5.31 crores. Remaining government grants about INR 5-6 crores pending.

qa_highlights.question: Residential project economics and revenue recognition?
qa_highlights.answer: Outlay about INR 45 crores over the 24-month project on owned land, revenue about INR 80 crores; revenue to be recognised on completion certificate as per standard.

risks_watch: Input cost volatility (cotton and other raw materials) and gradual pass-through could pressure the 14% EBITDA margin guidance.
Retail store economics still immature; most stores under one year old, and management withheld per-store revenue and EBITDA break-even data.
Store additions slowed: FY26 achieved about 26 against 35 guided; FY27 target of about 70 total depends on finding sites.
Working capital: inventory and debtors up about 25%; net cash flow from operations of about INR 93 crores versus PAT of INR 228 crores drew questions.
Preferential RPS issue timing depends on NCLT order (expected first week of June 2026), then about 3-4 months to issue shares.
Dombivali real estate project is outside core business; revenue recognition on completion and actual sellable area not yet confirmed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on core fabric business and overall growth, but cautious on retail economics and input prices, repeatedly declining to give store-level metrics or firm margin upgrades.
key_quotes: We will continue with our guidance of approximately 14% of EBITDA with the 150 basis points of drop due to retail.
So, we are very excited about this business going forward as well.
We don't look at the business as a quarterly business. We look at the guidance and the business as an overall annual business since it follows seasonality.
We are in the first few years of our retail journey, particularly in ZECODE and DEVO.

adds.what: About 26 new company-owned ZECODE/DEVO retail stores (to reach ~70 by FY27 end; 44 at Q4 FY26)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 12% with store expansion to ~70 (about 26 new COCO stores, ~INR 40 cr capex) and new ZECODE geographies, but no order book or utilisation data given, and management flagged input-cost and geopolitical risks, so backing is partial.
